relevance_note: P6 of the authors' cohort carries a de novo 3.576 Mb 6q23.3-q24.1 deletion, and 'The TNFAIP3 gene was involved in the deleted fragment in P6'; a literature-table patient (Table 3 row 1, ref [18]) has a 6q23.2-q24.3 deletion attributed by the cited report's title to TNFAIP3 haploinsufficiency.
method_note:
I read the full paper myself. A short Python script in my scratch directory then assembled the JSON, cutting table-row segments out of the paper text. I checked each segment against the tables, and the script checked every span verbatim. Tables 1 and 2 list patients as columns; the column used is headed 'P6' (sixth patient column). Table 3 lists patients as rows with no label column, so the person taken from it is 'Table 3 row 1'.
SCOPE. The cohort has 145 patients, 8 of them with chromosomal abnormalities (P1-P8). Only P6 has a TNFAIP3-involving variant: a de novo, heterozygous 3.576 Mb 6q23.3-q24.1 deletion (Table 1 lists 'TNFAIP3, IFNGR1, etc' as genes in the region). P6 gets a row; P1-P5, P7, P8 and the rest of the cohort are out of scope. P5's PTPN11 c.1508G > C belongs to an out-of-scope patient. The deletion also covers IFNGR1 and other genes. It is recorded as one CNV row under TNFAIP3, with no separate rows for other genes in the same deletion. P6's father and mother are included as tested relatives: Fig. 4a shows their NGS reads, and the text says the parents had no FUO and no chromosomal abnormalities. They have no variant rows.
LITERATURE TABLE. Table 3 row 1 (6q23.2-q24.3 del, Refs [18]) is included because reference [18] is printed with the title 'TNFAIP3 haploinsufficiency is the cause of autoinflammatory manifestations in a patient with a deletion of 13Mb on chromosome 6'. The paper's own text never says that TNFAIP3 lies inside that deletion, so this inclusion rests on the printed reference title. The other 18 literature patients have no stated TNFAIP3 link and are out of scope.
DIAGNOSIS LABELS. The paper never uses the terms HA20 or A20 haploinsufficiency for P6. The authors class P6 as inflammatory fever ('P6: inflammatory fever', Fig. 2) and say P6 'clinically manifested with early-onset s-JIA'.
SYMBOLS. The legends of Tables 1 and 3 do not define the '–' cells, so those cells are recorded as not reported. '+' is read as present; the text corroborates it for P6 (growth retardation, developmental delay, lymphadenectasis, arthritis). Table 2 arrows are read against the printed reference ranges.
GROUP STATEMENTS. Two P6 rows rest on group statements naming the six inflammatory-fever patients (P1-P6). (1) Pharyngitis/tonsillitis is excluded for P6 from 'occurred in 4/6 patients (P1-P4)'. (2) Hyperpyrexia is recorded as observed from 'These patients suffered from hyperpyrexia'. The parents' 'no FUO' comes from a statement about the parents of all eight patients. Oral ulcers for P6 are left not reported, although the text attributes recurrent oral aphthous ulcers only to P4 and P5; no statement says explicitly that the others lacked them.
CHECKLIST JUDGEMENTS. P6's pancytopenia, attributed to suspected HLH, is not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'. The perianal ulcers in Table 3 row 1 are not mapped to gastrointestinal or genital ulcers, because the site is anatomically ambiguous. The parents' 'no FUO' does not exclude 'recurrent fever'.
AGES. P6's age at last evaluation is her age at death (4.5 years); the Table 2 laboratory values were taken at 51 m. The '< 1y' onset in Table 3 row 1 is not converted to ISO 8601. n_patients_reported is null because the authors give no count of patients with a TNFAIP3 variant. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is true only through the literature patient from [18]; the paper does not say any of its own cohort patients were reported before.
INCONSISTENCY. The Results say the CNVs were 'verified with CGH (Fig. 3) or MLPA (Fig. 4c)'. But Fig. 3 (CGH) does not include P6, and the MLPA in Fig. 4c covers only P1. P6's deletion is shown only by NGS read depth (Fig. 4a). I found no contradictions about P6's clinical features.
